do_not_assume: A completion date alone means complete.
A prerequisite survives moving the Step Type to another program.
goal: A Step Program whose order, prerequisites and completion semantics match the intended journey.
steps: Define the journey’s Step Types and decide whether sequence is required, preferred or display-only.
Select the corresponding Completion Flow.
Configure statuses and identify which statuses are complete.
Configure each type’s prerequisites, repeatability and spans-time behavior.
Add only the Step Attributes needed for the operational record; enable Show in Grid or Show on Bulk where appropriate.
Test one participant record with the intended date and status combination.
Verify the change in Person History.
Inspect the Step’s current status.
Confirm that the status is configured as an **Is Complete** status in the Step Program.
Confirm that both the completion date and completion status are present.
If a workflow should have launched, inspect the program- or type-level trigger and installed Rock version.
Stop when both completion signals are correct and the expected downstream behavior has been rechecked. (Edit Step Programs)
title: Recipe: Configure a Step journey with reliable completion signals

do_not_assume: Do not assume Data View membership overrides prerequisites or repeat limits.
goal: Multiple selected people receive the intended Step data without silently losing per-person attribute differences.
steps: Choose either selected-person grid update or Step Program/Step Type bulk entry.
Confirm the target program, type, status and applicable date fields.
Apply shared attributes only when Show on Bulk is enabled and one value is correct for every selected person.
Enter differing attribute values separately for each person.
Verify sample records and their profile history.
Confirm the person currently qualifies for the Auto-Complete Data View.
Confirm the Steps Automation job has processed the Step Type.
Inspect unmet prerequisite Steps.
If a record already exists, inspect **Allow Multiple** before expecting another occurrence.
Do not assume Data View membership overrides prerequisites or repeat limits. (Edit Step Types)
title: Recipe: Bulk-record a Step

do_not_assume: Every person in the Data View receives a new record; prerequisites and repeat limits remain active. (Edit Step Types)
goal: The Steps Automation job creates or completes qualifying records while preserving journey rules.
steps: Build and validate the person Data View.
Assign it as the Step Type’s Auto-Complete Data View.
Inspect prerequisites and Allow Multiple.
Run or wait for the configured Steps Automation job according to the installation’s operating procedure.
Verify qualifying, prerequisite-blocked and already-completed examples.
Inspect the Step’s current status.
Confirm that the status is configured as an **Is Complete** status in the Step Program.
Confirm that both the completion date and completion status are present.
If a workflow should have launched, inspect the program- or type-level trigger and installed Rock version.
Stop when both completion signals are correct and the expected downstream behavior has been rechecked. (Edit Step Programs)
title: Recipe: Automate Step completion from a Data View

do_not_assume: Start date or frequency can be corrected later; both are locked after save. (Add a New Streak Type, Streaks Maps)
goal: A Streak Type calculates the intended cadence from the intended source.
steps: Define the activity source, target population, frequency and earliest applicable date.
Decide whether enrollment is required.
Decide whether Sync Linked Activity’s bidirectional behavior is appropriate.
Configure and inspect the occurrence map.
Enroll a small test population.
Verify engagement, non-engagement and exclusion examples.
Confirm the operational job timing before expanding use.
Distinguish an occurrence-map edit from an individual engagement- or exclusion-map edit.
For an individual map edit, save and refresh the page.
For an occurrence-map edit, confirm that the nightly cleanup job has run.
Inspect enrollment dates because earlier dates remain outside each person’s calculation. (Streak Type Detail, Manually Track Streaks)
title: Recipe: Build a Streak Type safely

do_not_assume: An exclusion removes or changes attendance.
goal: A bounded correction is made without unnecessarily rebuilding the entire Streak Type.
steps: Inspect the occurrence map and the person’s enrollment date.
Compare attendance with the engagement map.
Add or remove an engagement only if the map should differ from the source-driven result.
Add an individual exclusion when an absence should be ignored for that person.
Save and refresh.
Verify current streak, longest streak and engagement count.
Confirm the person’s enrollment date.
Inspect the occurrence map for eligible dates after enrollment.
Determine whether the engagement map contains participation.
If historical attendance should populate the map, consider an individual rebuild.
Before rebuilding, record any manual engagement-map changes because the rebuild deletes them. (Intro to Streak Enrollment, Rebuild Streaks Individually)
title: Recipe: Correct one person’s streak

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Attendance-derived streak data is regenerated at the smallest necessary scope.
steps: Decide whether the problem affects one enrollment or the entire Streak Type.
Record existing manual map adjustments in the affected scope.
Confirm the Streak Type start date and occurrence map.
Use individual rebuild for one person; use type rebuild only for a type-wide regeneration need.
Verify enrollment dates, maps, current streaks and longest streaks after completion.
Reapply only reviewed manual exceptions that remain valid.
title: Recipe: Rebuild a Streak with a controlled boundary

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: The intended people receive valid assessment requests and their completion state can be reviewed.
steps: For one person, use Request Assessment from the profile, select one or more assessments and provide the custom message.
For many people, use a communication that generates the assessment’s external URL from the public application root and each recipient’s URL-encoded person key.
Tell recipients that requests are also available from My Account.
Review pending and complete entries on person assessment histories.
Cancel an incorrect request only while it remains incomplete.
title: Recipe: Request and monitor assessments

do_not_assume: Similar-looking measurements across different assessments have the same meaning. (Intro to Assessments, Emotional Intelligence, Conflict Profile)
goal: A person Data View identifies people with a specified supported assessment result.
steps: Select the assessment and exact result measurement or attribute.
Choose the documented rating or result condition.
Build the person Data View filter.
Validate sample included and excluded records.
Use the resulting population for the separately governed grouping or reporting task.
title: Recipe: Build an assessment-result segment

do_not_assume: Achievement success overrides Step prerequisites or repeat limits. (Add Achievement Types, Achievement Type Advanced Settings, Configure Steps in Achievement Types)
goal: A successful Achievement produces the intended follow-up and journey record.
steps: Define the Achievement source, target and success conditions.
Choose either overachievement or capped accomplishments.
Configure start, success and failure workflows as needed.
Enable Add Step on Success.
Select the Step Program, Step Type and status.
Confirm that the target Step’s prerequisites and Allow Multiple behavior match recurring Achievement behavior.
Test start, success and failure paths with bounded records.
Verify the attempt, workflow result and generated Step independently.
title: Recipe: Connect an Achievement to workflows and Steps

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A context-valid reminder produces the intended communication or workflow at its reminder date.
steps: Define the Reminder Type’s entity and security.
Choose Communication or Workflow notification.
Configure note inclusion and automatic completion deliberately.
For Communication, select the system communication in the Process Reminders job.
For Workflow, configure the workflow to receive the supplied reminder-related attributes.
Include the type in job processing and set any per-entity limit.
Test a bounded reminder and verify delivery or workflow launch, completion behavior and header count.
title: Recipe: Configure Reminder processing

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Authorized subscribers receive the intended daily event without exposing related sensitive context.
steps: Define the event and its matching conditions.
Secure View permission to the intended subscribers.
Review the security of related notes, groups and represented records separately.
Enable the event in a test subscriber’s Following Settings.
Validate matching and non-matching examples.
Verify the next daily notification output.
title: Recipe: Configure a secure Following event

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Participants receive the intended actions while only approved responses appear publicly.
steps: Configure the schedule and any Data View, group or campus restrictions.
Preview the participant experience.
Open the intended question.
Monitor incoming responses.
Approve or reject responses requiring moderation.
Select the presenter question and campus filter.
Close the question when participation should end.
Verify graphical or word-cloud output from approved responses.
Confirm that the question is currently shown and not closed.
Confirm that the response was submitted to the intended experience.
If moderation is enabled, inspect whether the response awaits approval or was rejected.
Inspect campus filtering in the manager or presenter view.
If audience restrictions are involved, inspect the schedule’s Data View or group-membership condition. (Intro to Interactive Experiences, Use the Experience Manager)
title: Recipe: Operate a moderated Interactive Experience

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Guests or an existing group can register, and authorized operators can record attendance.
steps: Confirm the project’s underlying group and opportunity structure.
For a custom project type, verify inheritance, child-type allowance, schedule option, location mode and Finder inclusion.
Configure the external Finder for guest self-registration, or configure Sign-Up Register in Group mode for an existing group.
Pass the required project, location, schedule and group IdKeys.
Configure the attendance page with the required IdKeys and a `yyyy-MM-dd` occurrence date.
Configure the Group Attendance Reminder communication when reminder links are needed.
Verify the organization phone number on SMS-enabled registration and reminder communications.
Test with an account holding the intended project or group-type permissions.
For registration or reminder communication errors, confirm that an organization phone number is configured for the SMS-enabled system communication.
For a registration route, verify project, location, schedule and, when applicable, group IdKeys.
Remember that the project parameter represents the Sign-Up group.
For attendance, confirm the occurrence date uses `yyyy-MM-dd`.
Inspect project or group-type permissions before changing attendee records. (Configure Sign-Ups, Group Registration and Attendance for Sign-Ups, Configure Sign-Up Permissions)
title: Recipe: Configure a Sign-Up registration and attendance route
